canonical_claim: The three server-root control objects live under `gc/server-roots/<srid>/`: `owner` is a write-once identity anchor, `epoch` is a CAS-bumped monotone counter, and `mount` is a token-guarded lease body.; The server-root text objects are `cas_owner`, `cas_epoch`, and `cas_mount_lease`: the owner binds a server-root id to a server UUID, the epoch stores the monotone next writer epoch, and the mount lease stores the live holder and merged `min_active` state.; The durable per-server_root_id identity is built from three sticky objects under gc/server-roots/<server_root_id>/: owner (permanent, putIfAbsent once, binds server_root_id to one server_uuid_hex forever), epoch (permanent, CAS-bumped per writable open, a durable monotone writer_epoch counter never reissued), and mount (an expirable heartbeat lease, same-UUID reclaim only after expiry). The identity/fencing model has three durable layers with a fixed startup order: `OwnerProto`/owner is identity (write-once binding of `server_root_id` to `server_uuid`, clock-free, never deleted or reassigned, foreign UUID fails closed even if a lease is expired); `ServerEpochProto`/epoch is the durable monotone fence (CAS-bumped on each mount attempt, hands out a fresh `writer_epoch`, must survive lease expiry/reclaim, and a missing epoch over non-empty data is a reset hazard); `MountLeaseProto`/mount is liveness (renewed repeatedly, has wall-clock expiry/seq/hostname/pid diagnostics, reclaimable when expired or GC-fenced). Startup order is exactly owner then epoch then mount.
